title: Mixed-Acceleration ML Discovers Ruthenium Acidic OER Catalysts with 12× Lower Dissolution for Green Hydrogen
aiSystem: Mixed-Acceleration Active-Learning ML Platform (Univ. of Toronto)
whyItMatters: Published in Nature Catalysis, ML-guided mixed acceleration across 379 experiments discovered 7 ruthenium acidic OER catalysts surpassing the activity–stability Pareto frontier, cutting dissolution 12× vs RuO₂.
summary: Published in Nature Catalysis on January 6, 2026 (Vol. 9, Issue 1, pp. 28–36, doi:10.1038/s41929-025-01463-x), Yang Bai, Edward H. Sargent, Jason Hattrick-Simpers, and collaborators at the University of Toronto solved a central bottleneck in proton-exchange-membrane (PEM) green hydrogen electrolysis: replacing scarce, prohibitively expensive iridium oxygen-evolution catalysts with durable ruthenium oxides that resist rapid acidic dissolution. By pairing machine learning active search with high-throughput synthesis and electrochemical screening ("mixed acceleration") across just 379 multi-element oxide experiments, the closed-loop workflow discovered seven ruthenium-based catalysts surpassing the prior activity–stability Pareto frontier. The lead composition, Ru0.5Zr0.1Zn0.4Ox, achieved an overpotential of 194 mV at 10 mA/cm² while exhibiting 12-fold lower ruthenium dissolution than benchmark RuO2 in harsh acid.
technicalHighlights: Active-learning ML paired with high-throughput electrochemical screening explored multi-metal oxide space in 379 experiments to discover 7 catalysts beating the acidic OER activity–stability Pareto frontier.
Lead catalyst Ru0.5Zr0.1Zn0.4Ox delivered 194 mV overpotential at 10 mA/cm² with 12× lower ruthenium dissolution than RuO2 under corrosive acidic operation.
Directly addresses the iridium scarcity bottleneck limiting gigawatt-scale PEM green-hydrogen water electrolyzers.
caveats: Multi-thousand-hour industrial membrane-electrode-assembly durability at commercial current densities (>1 A/cm²) still requires scale-up engineering.

scoreRationale.foundational: Breaks the classic activity–stability trade-off in acidic oxygen-evolution electrocatalysis using multi-element ruthenium oxides discovered via closed-loop ML.
scoreRationale.ripple: Targets the single most critical precious-metal supply constraint (iridium) in global PEM green-hydrogen deployment.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature Catalysis with experimental synthesis, electrochemical activity, and ICP-MS dissolution measurements.
scoreRationale.velocity: Navigated a vast multi-metal compositional space to 7 Pareto-optimal catalysts in just 379 closed-loop experiments.
